## ⭐ Sharpened by PR #19405 — the in-code copy is FIXED, so the frozen registry text is now the ONLY stale one

When this card was filed, the two-filter enumeration existed in both the runtime source and the ADR-0087 registry. PR #19405 (ruling item 2 of #17667, landed `0862063ba7`) **corrected the in-code copy on its own initiative**, verified by this seat:

| | on the parent `6af29010b9` | on `main` `0862063ba7` |
|---|---|---|
| ``this door applies the `status` / `type` `` (two filters) | **present** | gone |
| ```status` / `type` / `enabled` filters`` (three) | absent | **present** |

⇒ ⭐ **this card's remaining subject is now exactly the frozen text and nothing else.** Measured on `origin/main`, `filters on \`status\` / \`type\`` still lives in:

- `packages/spec/src/api/package-api.zod.ts` (the source string)
- `packages/spec/src/migrations/registry.ts`
- `packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/retired-keys/18.api__ListInstalledPackagesRequest__limit.ts`
- `content/docs/references/api/package-api.mdx` (generated from the first)

⚠️ That makes the card **cleaner, ⛔ not more urgent**: the enumeration a reader hits while reading the *code* is now right, and what remains is a **retirement record** — which may legitimately be frozen as written. ⛔ The first act is still to decide whether a superseded passage inside a dated record is amended at all.

## ⛔ The declaration was this seat's error, and the review is upheld, 2026-09-21T15:50Z

The at-tier contract review of PR #19595 returned **FAIL** on **one** ground, and the ground is the claim above, not the work: record [`5762666543`](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectstack/pull/19595#issuecomment-5762666543), judging head `a755473aac4018b3974315940594b704bf139c7d`. Adopted verbatim by this seat; ⛔ not rewritten.

**Independence pair**, machine-readable on that record: `Implemented-by: claude/issue-19407-list-door-tombstone-enumerates-two-of-three` (a branch — the dev ran `mode:subagent`) · `Reviewed-by: session_01AmH9bKvGoLjiY86Q4Z3og2` (the adopting seat). Distinct kinds, so no SELF-REVIEW.

### What the declaration got wrong

⭐ Clause ② is the declaration 「**this PR puts a new key on a published payload**」. This PR puts **none**: `limit` and `cursor` stay `retiredKey()` tombstones typed `never`, `status` / `type` / `enabled` were all already declared, and the only published thing that moves is the **text** of a refusal message plus two generated mirrors of it.

⚠️ This seat declared `yes` on all three of round 16's dispatches uniformly, reasoning from the `--tier` output's **path** hint — 「`packages/spec/src/**` … the normal landing zone of a clause-② card」. ⛔ That is a **path** reading, and the tool says so in its own words: 「Clause ② is NOT reachable from paths … judged from the card CONTENT」. The content here is prose. ⇒ `no`.

### The consequence was mechanical, not cosmetic

`check-changeset-no-major.mjs`'s level axis refuses `yes` + `patch`, and `Check Changeset` on that head exited **1** on exactly that:

> ⛔ This PR declares clause-② `yes`, and it grades NO package whose `packages/**/src/**` it moves at `minor` or above. — `@objectstack/spec: patch`

⭐ **And the reviewer found why neither the dev's nor this seat's local sweep could see it**: the level axis reads the **pull_request payload**. The same command with no payload exits **0**, printing 「LEVEL AXIS: NOT APPLICABLE — this run has no pull_request to read a declaration from」. ⇒ a local derived-gate sweep reconciling 104 families reads green while the PR's own required job is red. ⛔ Not a dev failing.

### The remedy, and the route NOT taken

Route 2 — correct the declaration at its producer. This comment is that correction on the card side; the PR body's line is the dev's to fix.

⛔ **Route 1 is explicitly refused**: raising `@objectstack/spec` to `minor` would clear the red by publishing a **false widening signal** into a lockstep fixed group, for a diff that changes a comment and a string. ⛔ A gate cleared by making the repository say something untrue is not cleared.

**Carriers stripped at this same act** — `needs:contract-review` removed from PR #19595 and from this card, read back clean on both. A FAIL strips them exactly as a PASS does.

### What the review confirmed, so the patch round does not re-litigate it

The enumeration work is **right**, measured first-hand and not adopted: the door reads exactly three keys (`enabled` `:828`/`:845`, `status` `:837`, `type` `:840`) and no fourth. ⭐ The minimality claim is **reproducible, not asserted** — applying exactly two substitutions to the base string reproduces the head string byte-for-byte, and the load-bearing sentence 「no page was ever withheld and no continuation token was ever minted」 is present and byte-identical. The generated mirrors are the tooling's (`git status` empty after regeneration), and the published docs page was checked **against the door**, not against the source string.
